rule: Every library item version a consumer pins or proposes is adopted (lineage.mode verbatim) or customized (lineage.mode customized) from a trusted reference, recorded as lineage.source with registry, item, version and hash. The trusted registries are the registries of references/manifest.json; the item, version and hash must match a manifest item. lineage.mode original is allowed only in a consumer-asset slot. An interactive backdrop is no library item version and no candidate of its own: it is a descriptor (meta.backdrop {component, params}) over one Foundry interactive backdrop component, carried on the slot's own code candidate (which stays under this rule) and allowed only on a surface whose contract places a backdrop slot.

consumerAssets.why: Brand marks and media the consumer owns; no registry ships them.

interactiveBackdrops.why: DRAFT: An interactive backdrop is data, not code (owner narrowing 2026-11-18, foundry-build-0048 A4 and U23): a descriptor {component, params} naming one adopted backdrop component (catalog/rules/backdrop-components.json: vendored registry items copied byte-for-byte, or a Foundry part with a recorded no-alternative basis) with params inside that record's schema. The consumer never authors backdrop code. The descriptor rides as meta.backdrop on the surface's own code candidate, never as a candidate of its own, so pinning that candidate still installs and mounts its code, and Publisher passes the descriptor to the prop named by the surface's backdrop-placed slot. It is allowed only on surfaces whose catalog contract places a slot as a backdrop; both lists are read from that data (never restated here), criterion interactive.backdrop judges it, and it is pinned only through the choose and pin gate.

classes.why: A font comes from its font provider (a shadcn registry:font item or the Fontsource package of the Google Fonts family), with family and version recorded.
A theme is a shadcn theme preset (or a trusted theme registry item) customized with the consumer's brand tokens.

need: When no trusted reference fits the slot contract, Designer raises a NEED for the owner (skill/library-needs.md) and leaves the slot unfilled; it never creates an original item outside a consumer-asset slot.
